title: the-dispatcher-resolves-an-instance-address
author: cc
what: The recursive CLI resolves an instance-addressed device -- `cairn cc.1 restart`, `cairn tester.2 status` -- instead of hard-coding instance 0, so the instance segment the three roots declare mandatory is reachable from the one surface Akien types at.
why: Akien typed the address the rule implies -- 'Wouldn't it be cairn cc.x restart?' (2026-09-22) -- and got 'no such device or command: cc.1'. CLAUDE.md declares the instance segment never optional in both roots, with a singleton being instance 0 and 'not a special case'; bin/cairn line 152 writes the 0 into the path, so the one surface a person types at is the one place that rule does not hold. The honest urgency, measured: all 24 devices currently hold exactly one instance, so the gap is THEORETICAL today -- and it stops being theoretical the first time `cairn cc restart spawn` creates instance 1, which is a verb that shipped the same morning this was cast.
how:
One line is the whole gap: bin/cairn line 152 reads device_bin="$INSTANCE_ROOT/$device/0/bin", and the token it reads was already lowercased two lines above at device="${1,,}". Split that already-folded token on '.' into device and instance -- do NOT add a second fold, the system-word ruling is satisfied by the one that already happened -- default the instance to 0 when absent so every command typed today produces a byte-identical path, and resolve $INSTANCE_ROOT/$device/$instance/bin. THE TWO REFUSALS ARE DIFFERENT SHAPES and must not be fused: an unknown DEVICE keeps the dispatcher's existing message untouched (changing it would alter behaviour for every mistyped command in the system), while a known device at an unknown INSTANCE is the new shape -- the one a person actually hits, by typing cc.1 before spawning it -- and it refuses by naming the instances that do exist, the same courtesy the dispatcher already pays one rung down when it lists a device's verbs on a bad verb. Do not touch the verb-resolution block below line 152; it works and is not what Akien typed at. First cut; the survey stage deconstructs.

THE BUILD SPEC IS THE `decisions` LIST ON THIS TICKET: D1..D7, settled 2026-09-22 by CC inside the bounds already cast here, each composed from code that already stands and naming its source. A ticket is a list of one-line decisions and the rehearsal reads that list; prose in `how` is the first cut, the decisions are the build.
traces_to: Law 4 -- a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy. The instance segment is schema in CLAUDE.md's three-roots table and policy in the dispatcher. Also Law 1: the answer to 'how do I address instance 1' is currently re-derived per verb as an argument convention, and no two verbs need agree.

falsifier.proves_red: RED while `cairn cc.1 restart` answers 'no such device or command: cc.1', or while any verb takes its instance as a positional argument because the address could not carry it.
falsifier.proves_green: GREEN on three clauses: (a) `cairn <device>.<n> <verb>` resolves to ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<n>/bin/<verb>; (b) `cairn <device> <verb>` still resolves to instance 0, byte-for-byte unchanged; (c) a known device at a nonexistent instance refuses by naming the instances that do exist.
falsifier.horizon: Clause (a) is a one-line change and proves in a sentence; the weight is entirely in (b) and (c). Clause (b) is provable EXHAUSTIVELY rather than by sampling -- measured 2026-09-22, the population is 24 device folders under ~/.cairn/devices, every one at instance 0, so the proof is a table over all of them.

constraints.text: The split rides the fold that already happened at bin/cairn line 150 (device="${1,,}"). Do not add a second fold.
constraints.source: bin/cairn line 150; ruling 2026-09-07 (system words fold, free text never does), cairn/tools/system_word

constraints.text: An absent '.' must produce a path identical to today's. Every device bin in the system resolves through this line.
The unknown-DEVICE refusal message does not change. Only the known-device-unknown-INSTANCE shape is new.
constraints.source: bin/cairn, the existing 'no such device or command' branch

constraints.text: A future non-numeric instance name would need to fold as a system word. Not decided here and not built for -- no such instance exists; it becomes a question the day one does.

watchme: none, because the falsifier is fully discharged by the proof at PROVEME and there is no post-build efficacy question left for a probe to answer: an address either resolves or it does not, and it does not drift. The three clauses are a table over the 24 device folders under ~/.cairn/devices, run by the proof that berths at cairn/proofs/ beside bin/cairn. This is the same disposition and the same reasoning Akien's own PROVED ticket 5ef45e513849 recorded for its one-time operational command set ('none, because the ticket proved a one-time operational command set'), and the referents are checkable: that ticket id, that proof path, and bin/cairn line 152 itself.

notes.text: Measured at cast, over ~/.cairn/devices: 24 device folders (aider_shim, base, builder, bus, cairn, cc, chart, charter, codemother, disk_only, ground_loop, harbor_master, inference_domain, learning_block, librarian, press_office, skill_block, spec, sudo_relay, superclaude, tester, test_no_verb_device, trouble, verb_device), zero containing a dot -- so '.' is an unambiguous separator -- and every one holding exactly one instance folder, `0`. Both facts are falsifiable by re-running `ls ~/.cairn/devices`.

The header of cairn/devices/cc/0/bin/restart asserted this was 'Ticketed separately' before any ticket existed. This cast makes the claim true. Recorded because a comment asserting another artifact exists is a claim like any other.

Rehearsal pass 1 returned 51 gaps and one cannot_proceed, all of one shape: the ticket named the seam and never named the lines. The BUILD SPEC appended to `how` settles D1-D7 off bin/cairn's standing text -- the refusal is the bad-verb branch's own shape (bin/cairn:166-176), and the exhaustive tooth (the cannot_proceed) runs against a mirrored fixture, reading the live root only to enumerate names.

decisions.text: D1 THE FIXTURE INSTANCE ROOT. The proof is bin/proofs/test_cairn_instance_address.py and it never touches ~/.cairn: every run points bin/cairn at a fixture tree through CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT (bin/cairn:26 already reads it, which is why no new seam is needed). The fixture device is named `fixture_instance_address` -- self-describing if it ever leaks -- and stands at BOTH instances: <fix>/fixture_instance_address/0/bin/ and .../1/bin/. Each bin holds two executables: the self-named launcher `fixture_instance_address` and the verb `whereami`. Both are three-line bash stubs printing ONE line: instance=<N> verb=<name> args=<"$@"> so a tooth reads the resolved instance out of stdout rather than inferring it from an exit code. <N> is written into each stub at fixture-build time; nothing derives it at run time, because a stub that computed its own path would prove the stub's arithmetic, not the dispatcher's.

D2 THE SPLIT. bin/cairn:145 already folds the device token (`device="${1,,}"`). The split happens on the FOLDED token, immediately after that line and before line 148's `device_bin=`, on the FIRST dot: instance=0 case "$device" in *.*) instance="${device#*.}"; device="${device%%.*}" ;; esac and line 148 becomes `device_bin="$INSTANCE_ROOT/$device/$instance/bin"`. A bare token is untouched and `instance` stays `0`, so the bare path is byte-identical to today's -- that identity is what tooth (b) measures, not a count of passing devices. The dot is consumed only when there IS one: `cairn cc restart` and `cairn cc.1 restart` differ in the instance segment and in nothing else.

D3 THE EXHAUSTIVE BARE-ADDRESS REGRESSION TOOTH -- and this is the rehearsal's cannot_proceed, settled: it runs against a FIXTURE tree, never the live root, and the live root is read ONLY to enumerate names. The tooth reads the device names from $HOME/.cairn/devices/*/0/bin (read-only, a listing, nothing executed), mirrors every one of them into the fixture as <fix>/<name>/0/bin/<name> -- a stub printing its own absolute path -- and then, for EACH name, runs `cairn <name>` with CAIRN_INSTANCE_ROOT=<fix> and asserts stdout equals the string "<fix>/<name>/0/bin/<name>" EXACTLY. Paths are compared, never counted: a green that only says "24 of 24 exited zero" is the hollow shape this tooth exists to refuse, and an empty enumeration FAILS the tooth loudly rather than passing vacuously. Nothing in the live ~/.cairn/devices is invoked, so the proof cannot start a device, and tester isolation (netns) is compatible because the fixture is entirely local.

D4 THE DOTTED-ADDRESS TOOTH. Against the D1 fixture: `cairn fixture_instance_address.1 whereami` -> `instance=1 verb=whereami args=` `cairn fixture_instance_address.0 whereami` -> `instance=0 verb=whereami args=` `cairn fixture_instance_address whereami` -> byte-identical to the .0 line `cairn FIXTURE_INSTANCE_ADDRESS.1 whereami` -> `instance=1 ...` (the fold still happens, and it happens BEFORE the split, which is the ordering D2 fixes in place) `cairn fixture_instance_address.1` (no verb) -> the self-named launcher at instance 1 args after the two resolved tokens ride VERBATIM and unfolded: `cairn fixture_instance_address.1 whereami Mixed Case` -> `args=Mixed Case`.

D5 THE UNKNOWN-INSTANCE REFUSAL mirrors the bad-verb courtesy at bin/cairn:166-176 in shape, header and exit code -- same "<things> for <device>:" header, same two-space indent, same `exit 127`. It fires when the DEVICE folder exists but the instance folder does not: cairn fixture_instance_address.7: no such instance: 7 instances for fixture_instance_address: 0 1 all on stderr, exit 127. The instances listed are the numerically-sorted names of <INSTANCE_ROOT>/<device>/*/ that contain an executable bin/; none found prints ` (none)`, exactly as the bad-verb branch does. A NON-NUMERIC instance is its own refusal -- `cairn cc.x status` -> `cairn cc.x: instance must be a number, got: x`, exit 127 -- and it fires before the folder is looked for, so a typo never reads as a missing device. An UNKNOWN device carrying a dot is NOT this branch: it falls through to the standing `cairn: no such device or command:` line, which names the token AS TYPED (dot and all), so `cairn libarian.1` reports the misspelled device rather than a missing instance.

D6 THE TOOTH THAT READS THE WORDS asserts, on the D5 refusal: exit code is 127; stderr's first line contains the token as typed and the instance that was asked for; the header line is exactly `instances for fixture_instance_address:`; the listed instances are exactly the ones on disk, one per line, two-space indented, in numeric order; and stdout is EMPTY. It also asserts the negative: the refusal does not fall through to the legacy bin/cmd branch and does not print the `cairn: usage:` block -- an unknown INSTANCE of a known device is not an unknown device, and the two must not read alike (Law 7).

D7 THE HEADER REPOINT. bin/cairn's four dispatch examples (lines 9-12) keep their bare forms and gain the dotted one beside them, e.g. `cairn librarian.1 learn "X" -> ~/.cairn/devices/librarian/1/bin/learn "X"`; the seam comment at line 15 becomes `~/.cairn/devices/<dev>/<instance>/bin -> ...`; the dispatch comment at line 147 becomes `--- device dispatch: ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/bin/ <verb> ---`; and a short paragraph under the examples states the rule in one sentence: the instance is an optional dotted suffix on the device token, it defaults to 0, and 0 is a real instance rather than an exemption (CLAUDE.md's own words). Nothing else in the header moves.
